thread:
Maria: quick check — a customer submitted a data deletion request. which log stores/streams do we need to wipe to be compliant? thinking app logs, traces, and any cache snapshots.
Jonathan: depends on the customer scope. do we have their org id or user id? we need that to find related events.
Maria: org=acme-inc, user ids start with acme:. they said logs + traces + any stored request/response blobs.
Sree: please file a ticket in backlog with the deletion request + consent proof. operations can't act without it.
InfraBot: runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/log-retention-delete — steps listed for s3 logs, datadog traces, and redis caches. :robot_face:
Sean: TL;DR: s3 access-logs (bucket logs/), app-logs (s3://redwood-logs/acme-inc/), datadog traces (trace-id tags), and redis ttl keys. default TTLs: app logs 90d, traces 30d.
Alyssa: also check nightly snapshots/backups. db backups are stored in snapshots-bkt/YYYY-MM-DD — they require an ops ticket to rotate/delete.
Maria: can someone paste the exact aws cli to delete the s3 prefix? I'll run it with infra approval.
Jonathan: run locally with dryrun first. example:

```
aws s3 rm s3://redwood-logs/acme-inc/ --recursive --profile redwood-ops --dryrun
```

then remove --dryrun to actually delete.
Sree: for datadog traces, we can't delete individual traces retroactively. we can request expunge from datadog support — need security approval and the ticket id.
Alyssa: for Redis cached responses we can evict keys by prefix. example:

```
redis-cli -h cache-prod --scan --pattern "acme:*" | xargs -L 100 redis-cli -h cache-prod del
```

use with care (ops only).
Maria: who needs to sign off before we delete? security + infra + compliance?
Jonathan: yep — security + infra approval, and compliance confirmation of legal basis. tag @compliance-team in the ticket.
compliance-team-bot: Received ticket RED-4589. Assigned to compliance for verification. Please include proof of user request and scope.
Maria: noted — I'll attach the deletion request and start the ops ticket. pinging here once compliance clears to schedule window.
Sean: also add a rollback note: we can't undelete s3 once removed. consider exporting a hashed audit copy (no PII) if legal requires.
Maria: thanks everyone, will update when we have approvals. :thumbsup:
